parts.title: Hydraulic Cylinder
parts.body: 27SiMn alloy steel (GB/T 3077), rated for 60–75 MPa system pressure and 300–620 tonnes of pressing force.

parts.title: Oil Pressure Plate
parts.body: Transfers the cylinder’s force evenly over the whole seed cake, so pressure reaches every seed uniformly instead of concentrating in the centre.

parts.title: Material Bucket
parts.body: Q690 high-strength steel, welded and nickel-plated inside and out. Strip-slotted walls release oil faster than a conventional drilled barrel, with no bare metal touching the seed.

parts.title: Oil Outlet
parts.body: Pressed oil collects here after draining through the bucket walls and runs straight into the tray below; the outlet is nickel-plated for food-grade contact.

parts.title: Control Panel
parts.body: Pressure gauges, adjustable cycle timer and safety interlocks grouped on one button-controlled panel.

parts.title: Directional Control Valve
parts.body: Electroplated valve block with enlarged ports for fast, smooth cycle switching.

parts.title: Hydraulic Oil Tank
parts.body: Built-in oil tank with filter and cooling keeps system oil clean and at a stable temperature.

faqs.q: How do I pick the right press model for my seeds?
faqs.a: Start from your raw material and your daily output target. Small shops working sesame or peanut usually run the HN300 or HN325; hard, low-oil seeds such as walnut or camellia call for the HN365 or above, while the HN426 and HN500 fit high-volume plants. Send us your seed type and target capacity and we will size the machine honestly — not upward.

faqs.q: What is the difference between cold pressing and hot pressing?
faqs.a: Cold pressing skips roasting, keeps oil temperature low and preserves natural nutrients and a light flavor preferred by premium markets, though the yield is smaller and downstream refining is often needed. Hot pressing roasts the seed first, extracting more oil with a stronger aroma for mainstream cooking oil. Every Haonuo model runs both processes.

faqs.q: How long does production take after I order?
faqs.a: Standard configurations are normally completed within 15–25 working days after the deposit arrives; custom setups may take 30–40 days depending on workshop load. Your confirmed loading window is written into the proforma invoice.

faqs.q: Do you provide installation and operator training?
faqs.a: Most single-press buyers install the machine themselves using the printed English manual and our online support. For complete lines, a Haonuo engineer can travel to your site for installation and training; the buyer covers flights, visa, accommodation and a daily service fee.

faqs.question: What is a cold press oil machine?
faqs.answer: A cold press oil machine extracts oil from seeds at temperatures below 60°C, helping retain the natural nutrients, flavor, and aroma of the oil. Unlike hot press methods that heat seeds to 120-180°C, cold pressing uses hydraulic pressure alone to extract oil, making it well-suited for producing premium, unrefined oils such as virgin coconut oil, cold-pressed sesame oil, and walnut oil. Haonuo's cold press oil machines deliver professional-grade extraction. Cold press yields are typically somewhat lower than hot pressing but produce higher-quality, premium-priced oils.

faqs.question: What is the difference between cold press and hot press?
faqs.answer: Cold press operates below 60°C helping retain nutrients, natural flavor, and aroma, while hot press heats seeds to 120-180°C which increases yield but may reduce oil quality. Cold-pressed oils are premium, unrefined products that typically command higher market prices than refined oils, though actual premiums vary significantly by market, region, and oil type. Hot-pressed oils require chemical refining and are suitable for bulk cooking oil production. For premium and organic oil markets, cold pressing is often preferred.

faqs.question: What seeds can be cold pressed?
faqs.answer: Most oil seeds can be cold pressed including sesame, peanut, coconut, walnut, almond, sunflower, flaxseed, mustard seed, rapeseed, tea seed, apricot kernel, and more. Hard-shell materials like walnut and apricot kernel benefit especially from cold pressing with high-pressure hydraulic presses. Coconut for VCO (Virgin Coconut Oil) and sesame for premium cooking oil are the most popular cold-pressed oils globally.

faqs.question: Is cold-pressed oil better?
faqs.answer: Cold-pressed oil generally retains more of certain nutrients, natural flavor, and aroma compared to hot-pressed or refined oils. Some vitamins and antioxidants may be reduced during high-temperature processing, though the degree varies by oil type and processing method. Cold-pressed oils are not processed with chemical refining agents. However, the chemical profile of any oil depends on the quality and handling of the raw material. While the yield may be slightly lower, the typically higher market value of cold-pressed oils makes cold pressing potentially more profitable for producers targeting premium and organic markets, though actual price premiums vary significantly.

faqs.question: What is the yield of cold press oil machine?
faqs.answer: Yield varies by seed type: coconut 55-65%, sesame 42-50%, peanut 38-45%, walnut 50-60%, sunflower 40-48%, flaxseed 30-38%, rapeseed 35-42%. Haonuo's hydraulic cold press machines with bar-type slotted barrel design achieve approximately 2-3% higher yields than traditional drilled barrel presses (based on Haonuo factory tests with graded sesame and peanut at 6-8% moisture; results vary with seed variety and preparation), minimizing the yield gap between cold and hot pressing methods.

faqs.question: What is a hydraulic oil press machine?
faqs.answer: A hydraulic oil press machine uses hydraulic pressure to extract oil from seeds and nuts. Unlike screw presses that generate heat through friction, hydraulic presses apply uniform static pressure at controlled temperatures, making them well-suited for cold pressing premium oils like sesame, walnut, and coconut oil. The process preserves natural nutrients, flavor, and aroma.

faqs.question: How does a hydraulic oil press work?
faqs.answer: The machine uses a hydraulic pump to generate high pressure (up to 75 MPa) which drives a piston into a barrel filled with prepared oil seeds. The pressure squeezes oil out through a slotted barrel while the compressed seed cake remains inside. A typical pressing cycle takes 40-90 minutes. The microcomputer control system automates the entire process from pressing to cake discharge.

faqs.question: What seeds can a hydraulic oil press process?
faqs.answer: Hydraulic oil presses can process 50+ types of oil seeds including sesame, peanut, coconut, walnut, almond, sunflower, flaxseed, mustard, rapeseed, tea seed, soybean, cottonseed, apricot kernel, and more. Different models are optimized for different seed types — smaller models for sesame and soft seeds, higher-pressure models for hard-shell nuts like walnut and almond.

faqs.question: What is the oil yield of a hydraulic oil press?
faqs.answer: Oil yield varies by seed type: sesame 42-50%, peanut 38-45%, coconut 55-65%, walnut 50-60%, rapeseed 35-45%, sunflower 40-48%. Haonuo hydraulic presses use a proprietary bar-type slotted barrel design that achieves approximately 2-3% higher yield than traditional drilled barrel presses (based on Haonuo factory tests with graded sesame and peanut at 6-8% moisture; results vary with seed variety and preparation), with residual oil in cake as low as 6-8%.

Request a quote and receive a detailed quotation including machine price, shipping, and estimated duties within 24 hours.

faqs.question: What is the difference between cold press and hot press?
faqs.answer: Cold press operates below 60°C preserving nutrients, natural flavor, and aroma — well-suited for premium oils like sesame, walnut, and virgin coconut oil. Hot press involves roasting seeds before pressing, which increases yield slightly but may alter flavor and reduce nutritional value. Hydraulic oil presses are naturally suited for cold pressing because they apply static pressure without friction-generated heat.

faqs.question: Can the machine run on a generator?
faqs.answer: Yes, Haonuo hydraulic presses only need 2.2 KW motor power, making them fully compatible with a 5-7 KVA generator. This makes them well-suited for areas with unstable or no grid electricity, such as rural Nigeria, Kenya, and other regions across Africa and Southeast Asia.
